## Week in Review — 2026-10-26 (period 19–25 October 2026)

**Date check:** `TZ=America/Toronto date +%F` → 2026-10-26, a Monday. Period 2026-10-19 → 2026-10-25.

### Counts
12 developments · 5 connections · 8 open questions · 10 figures · 8 calendar items.

### Storylines
**Updated with a dated snapshot (8):** agents-going-wrong, ai-enabled-hacking, ai-weapons-targeting, anthropic-pentagon-split, china-distillation-export-controls, compute-money, pacing-frontier-ai, regulating-frontier-ai-us. Each got new tracked figures; six got new open questions.

**Not updated (1):** mathematicians-vs-labs — nothing filed under it this week. Last snapshot 2026-10-19, last filed item 2026-10-16, so the four-week dormancy test does not yet hold. Left live.

**Marked dormant:** none. **Resolved:** none — no tracked question was settled by a documented event this week. 9 live, cap is 12.

**Proposed (no file created):** `ai-stack-supply-chain` — "The AI tooling stack as the target". Frame: compromises of the gateways, proxies and hosting platforms that hold other people's model credentials. Admission test: three developments across two weeks (OpenCode's API-key breach, 16–19 Oct; the LiteLLM 1.107.0 hijack and Railway's workspace breach, both 21 Oct; Microsoft's and Wiz's analyses, 21–23 Oct), and it could be settled by a named attribution or an industry credential-handling standard. It is distinct from ai-enabled-hacking, which tracks AI as the attacker's tool rather than as the thing attacked.

### Coverage gaps
No days in the period lacked a daily file — all seven, plus today's, were present.

### Sources I could not reach
- `openai.com/index/*` — HTTP 403 to both WebFetch and `scripts/fetch.js`. Every OpenAI figure in the edition rests on secondary accounts, and the edition says so.
- `media.defense.gov` Project Agincourt PDF and the war.gov release — 403 both ways. The letter's content rests on NewsNation and SOFX, stated in the item.
- `beckershospitalreview.com` — 403 both ways; its two quotes were re-verified against the AHA's own 19 October letter, which is what the edition cites.
- Seven links drew bot-blocking WARNs from the link checker (Sophos, Yahoo Finance, both SEC Meta filings, Breaking Defense, Times of Israel, SK hynix 6-K). All seven were confirmed open by hand — six via `scripts/fetch.js` (HTTP 200), Times of Israel via WebFetch. Zero link errors.

### Dropped
Anthropic's three new copyright suits (Canadian publishers, Elvis rightsholders, the lyrics fair-use hearing) and the Texas AG suit as a standalone development, both for the 12-item cap. The Texas suit is carried in full in the regulating-frontier-ai-us snapshot. Nothing was dropped for failure to verify.

### What the validators and fact-check flagged
Validators: initially 14 developments (cap 12) — fixed by merging the two Anthropic agent items and dropping the Texas development; one banned phrase ("could mean" in my own prose); one connection number ("4" in "Log4J") absent from the joined items; six hedge warnings; three edition attributions that matched no source URL. All fixed; final run is **0 errors, 0 warnings** on all three validators.

Fact-check: 24 findings, all 24 fixed. Two were substantive errors:
- The Storm-0940 item claimed "the two accounts differ and neither source explains the gap" between 151,000 and 111,000 failed logons. False — 111,000 is the 11 October subset of the 151,000+ total and Microsoft's own post states the relationship. Rewritten.
- The fired OpenAI researcher was named Marcin Korbak; the WSJ says **Tomek** Korbak. Corrected.

The rest: seven claims traceable to no listed source (Senator Murphy's call for an investigation, the Gecko Robotics contract conflict, China Daily and Treasury press-release material) were cut or had their sources added; eight quotations were not verbatim or were credited to the wrong publisher (Amazon, Wiz, LiteLLM ×2, x402/THN, OFAC spelling, Zscaler via The Record, Huang's $50 billion as CNBC narration rather than his words); METR's "coverage" figures were misread as coverage when they are *eligibility* shares with a model-strength qualifier — corrected in the week file and in the pacing-frontier-ai snapshot and figure; three unattributed causal inferences were re-attributed or removed; and one overstatement ("no second sensor network confirming it") was corrected — BleepingComputer reports Expel's Marcus Hutchins confirming Karimi's finding.

### Commit, push, email
- Edition commit: **40ece1fd5e90cc2452bc1cf83e63eb138ee7f7d6** (`data/2026-10-26.week.json`, `data/2026-10-26.week.host.json`, `storylines/`, `trace/`).
- Trace commits: b2e1a16, then **a14585ea64e5d454c9df7df7087429d1c209142f**.
- **Push: succeeded**, but not on the first attempt. The working tree was on a detached HEAD, so `git push origin main` was rejected as non-fast-forward against a local `main` that was two commits behind. I reattached `main` to the new commit and pushed cleanly (7b84d14..40ece1f). No pull request.
- **Email: sent** to [email redacted], message id `1a178b46102c6423`, with the subject, HTML and plain text from `site/email/2026-10-26.week.*` passed verbatim.

### One failure to flag
I sent the email before the page was live. I polled `https://aiedgebriefing.com/week/2026-10-26/` for roughly 40 minutes and it was still 404 at send time. Deploy run 40340514596 was `in_progress` with no failure throughout — the previous weekly run took 48 minutes, and my own trace push restarted the clock. Per §5 I sent rather than risk not sending, so the "Read the full week in review" link will 404 until the deploy finishes. The plain-text body carries the entire edition, so the content reached the reader regardless.

Also outside the period but worth your attention: **Anthropic's public Form S-1 landed on EDGAR this morning (26 October, file 333-299633)**. I noted the filing in the compute-money snapshot without figures and left the tracked question open; the numbers belong to next week's edition.
